answer: Every new identity begins below a cold-start cliff: no payout for the first thirty epochs, however much it stakes, because the timestamp anchor that ages reputation cannot be bought forward. Past the cliff, weight accrues only against unbroken umber-inked work history, and any gap of three silent epochs drops the account into the canyon, forcing it to re-climb the full cliff from zero. A farm spinning a thousand aliases therefore pays a thousand thirty-epoch waits, and nothing shortens a wait; time is the one cost an attacker cannot parallelise, while honest agents climb once and stay.
